title: Cusco, the Best City in the Americas
summary: Places that have become—or are about to become—the favorite of travelers from all over the world, who dream of visiting Peru because of all the stories they’ve heard and the photos they see every day on social media.
imageAlt: Cusco, the best city in the Americas
author: peruwonderstours
body:
That’s right! Cusco has once again been recognized as one of South America’s top tourist destinations in 2025. The Imperial City has received multiple international awards highlighting its historical, cultural and natural riches.
🏆 Recent awards
Travel + Leisure: For the second year in a row, readers of this prestigious US magazine voted Cusco the Best City in Central and South America, with a score of 87.47 out of 100. This award highlights its unique blend of Inca and colonial architecture, its vibrant culture and its exquisite cuisine.
Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Awards 2025: Cusco was named the Best Destination in South America, cementing its position as a must-visit for travelers seeking authentic and memorable experiences.
World destination ranking 2025: The city ranked 13th among the best tourist destinations in the world, the highest in Latin America. This recognition underlines the majesty of its Inca legacy and its importance as the gateway to Machu Picchu.
✨ Why does Cusco keep shining?
Cusco offers a unique experience that combines:
Historical and cultural heritage: From the imposing fortress of Sacsayhuamán to the Temple of the Sun (Qoricancha), the city is living testimony to Inca civilization and its fusion with colonial architecture.
Access to natural wonders: It’s the starting point for exploring the Sacred Valley of the Incas, the Rainbow Mountain and, of course, the enigmatic citadel of Machu Picchu.
Exceptional cuisine: Visitors can enjoy traditional dishes such as roast cuy (guinea pig), quinoa soup and a range of culinary fusions that reflect Peru’s diversity.
Vibrant festivals: Events such as Inti Raymi (the Festival of the Sun) and Corpus Christi offer a deep immersion in ancestral traditions and Andean spirituality.
These awards reinforce Cusco’s position as a world-class destination, ideal for anyone looking for a combination of adventure, history and culture in a spectacular setting.

title: The Cusco Tourist Ticket (Boleto Turístico)
summary: COSITUC (Comité de Servicios Integrados Turísticos Culturales Cusco) is the body responsible for collecting, managing and distributing the funds raised from sales of the Cusco Tourist Ticket. COSITUC is made up of the Provincial Municipality of Cusco, the Cusco Directorate of Culture and the Di…
imageAlt: Information about the Cusco Tourist Ticket
author: peruwonderstours
body:
Also known as the B.T.C., the Cusco Tourist Ticket (Boleto Turístico del Cusco) gives you entry to 16 places of interest in the city of Cusco, the surrounding area and nearby valleys such as the South Valley and the Sacred Valley of the Incas.
WHO CHARGES THIS ENTRANCE FEE?
COSITUC (Comité de Servicios Integrados Turísticos Culturales Cusco) is the body responsible for collecting, managing and distributing the funds raised from sales of the Cusco Tourist Ticket. COSITUC is made up of the Provincial Municipality of Cusco, the Cusco Directorate of Culture and the Regional Directorate of Foreign Trade and Tourism.
TYPES OF TOURIST TICKETS:
Comprehensive Tourist Ticket (Boleto Turístico Integral):
It is valid for 10 calendar days and lets you visit 16 tourist sites in Cusco. Here is a list of the sites it includes:
Regional Historical Museum
PukaPukara
Museum of Contemporary Art
Tambomachay
Museum of Popular Art
Pisac
Qorikancha Site Museum
Ollantaytambo
Qosqo Center of Native Art
Chinchero
Monument to Inca Pachacutec
Moray
Sacsayhuaman
Tipon
Q’enqo
Piquillacta
Partial Tourist Tickets:
You can buy the Cusco Tourist Ticket in partial form, depending on the sites you want to visit. To do so, choose one of the following 3 circuits:
Circuit I: This ticket is valid for 1 day and gives you entry to the archaeological sites in the Sacsayhuaman Archaeological Park, which are:
Sacsayhuaman
Qenqo
Tambomachay
PukaPukara
Circuit II: This ticket is valid for 2 days and gives you entry to the attractions in Cusco’s historic center and the South Valley, which are:
Regional Historical Museum
Museum of Contemporary Art
Museum of Popular Art
Qorikancha Site Museum
Qosqo Center of Native Art
Monument to Inca Pachacutec
Tipón Archaeological Park
Pikillacta Archaeological Park
Circuit III: This ticket is valid for 2 days and gives you entry to the archaeological sites in the Sacred Valley of the Incas. They are:
Pisac
Ollantaytambo
Chinchero
Moray

CONDITIONS:
The tourist ticket is personal and non-transferable, and you can only enter each site once within the validity period of the ticket you bought.
Comprehensive or partial Cusco Tourist Ticket for FOREIGNERS: This ticket is for the general public. You must show your passport or ID card both when buying it and when entering the tourist sites.
Comprehensive or partial Cusco Tourist Ticket for NATIONAL visitors: This is a discounted ticket exclusively for Peruvian visitors or residents. Holders must prove their status with a valid national ID card (DNI) or, for residents, a foreign resident card (carné de extranjería), and must carry it when entering the tourist sites.
Comprehensive or partial Cusco Tourist Ticket for FOREIGN STUDENTS: This ticket is for foreign students who can prove their status with a valid international student card (International Student Identity Card, or ISIC). They must be 25 years old or younger and must carry the card when entering the tourist sites.
Comprehensive or partial Cusco Tourist Ticket for PERUVIAN STUDENTS: This is a discounted ticket for Peruvian students. Holders must prove their status with a valid student card issued by SUNEDU (Peru’s National Superintendence of Higher University Education) and must carry it when entering the tourist sites.
CHILDREN, both Peruvian and foreign, are free up to age 9; from 10 to 17 they pay the student rate and must show an ID document proving their age. From 18 to 25, visitors pay the student rate upon presenting a student card (Peruvians) or ISIC card (foreigners); in all cases, the document must be valid.
WHERE CAN I BUY THE CUSCO TOURIST TICKET?
The Cusco Tourist Ticket cannot be bought or reserved online and has no availability limit, so you can buy it on the day of your visit. You can buy it at any of the following locations in Cusco:
Address: Av. El Sol 103 (Galerías Turísticas). Opening hours: Monday to Sunday, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
At all the sites included in the Tourist Ticket (except the Museum of Contemporary Art and the Pachacutec Monument).

title: Useful Facts About Peru
summary: General travel information about Peru: cities, weather, festivals, food, tourism, transport, currency, visas and travel distances. Peru is one of the leading tourist destinations in South America.
author: peruwonderstours
body:
Peru is located in the central western part of South America, on the shores of the Pacific Ocean. With approximately 30 million inhabitants, it covers 1,285,215.60 square kilometers and is the third-largest country in South America after Brazil and Argentina.
Politically, the country is organized into 24 regions, not including the Constitutional Province of Callao, and it is divided geographically into 3 major regions (coast, highlands and jungle).
Lima is the capital of Peru and the country’s largest city, followed by Arequipa, given its demographic and economic importance. Peru has two official languages: Spanish and Quechua, the language of the Inca Empire. It is possible to communicate in English in popular tourist areas.
The Andes mountain range runs through the country from south to north, parallel to the coast, forming the highland region.
Peru’s highest peak is Huascarán (6,768 m (22,200 ft)), located in the Cordillera Blanca, the main and highest branch of the Western Cordillera of the Andes and an ideal place for all kinds of adventure sports.
Weather in Peru
COAST:
Temperatures can reach 28°C (82°F) during the summer (December–April); the rest of the year, temperatures can drop to 14°C (57°F) with 90% humidity.
HIGHLANDS:
The rainy season runs from December to April, with temperatures ranging from 20°C to 5°C (68°F to 41°F); from May to November there are sunny days and very cold nights. This is the best time of year to visit the attractions of the Peruvian highlands.
JUNGLE:
The jungle has a tropical climate—hot, humid and rainy—with annual temperatures above 30°C (86°F).
Religion in Peru
Peru is one of the most religious countries in the world. Most of the population is Catholic, although there is broad tolerance of all faiths.
Currency and payment
The currency is the Nuevo Sol (S/.), with its multiples and fractions circulating as coins of 10, 20 and 50 céntimos and 1, 2 and 5 Nuevos Soles. There are banknotes of 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 Nuevos Soles. US dollars and euros are accepted at tourist businesses at the day’s exchange rate.
Most credit cards are accepted, such as Diners Club, Visa, MasterCard and American Express. Traveler’s checks have limitations, so check beforehand whether they are accepted.
Time in Peru
Peru is 5 hours behind GMT (Greenwich Mean Time). For reference, when it is noon in Peru, the time in other cities is:
Lima, capital of Peru (12:00)
New York (13:00)
Madrid ()
London (14:00)
Buenos Aires (14:00)
Paris (19:00)
Tokyo (02:00)*
Sydney (03:00)*
Santiago de Chile (13:00)
Rio de Janeiro (14:00)
Holidays in Peru
January 1 – New Year’s Day.
February 3 – Pisco Sour Day.
March, toward the end of the month – Holy Week.
May 1 – Labor Day.
June 15 – Andean Song Day.
July 24 and 25 – Anniversary of Huaraz.
July 28 and 29 – Peru’s Independence Day.
August 30 – Santa Rosa de Lima.
October 8 – Battle of Angamos.
November 1 – All Saints’ Day.
December 8 – Immaculate Conception.
December 25 – Christmas.
Food and drink in Peru
Peruvian cuisine is very diverse. The most famous traditional dishes are fish and seafood ceviche (“cooked” in lime juice), lomo saltado (stir-fried beef), anticuchos (grilled skewers), arroz con pollo (rice with chicken), ají de gallina (creamy chili chicken), pollo a la brasa (rotisserie chicken) with fries, pachamanca (meat and vegetables cooked underground with hot stones), picante de cuy (spicy guinea pig) and fried trout.
Don’t forget to try the authentic national drink, the Pisco Sour, the world-famous cocktail made with pisco, lime, egg whites and sugar.
Throughout Peru there are many restaurants serving a variety of regional, national and international dishes.
Tourist visas
Visas are not required for most citizens of the Americas and Western Europe. Citizens of Ecuador, Bolivia and Chile do not need a visa or passport to enter certain regions of the country. In this case, the permitted stay is 90 days, which can be extended by the immigration authorities.
Your passport must be valid for at least 90 days on arrival in Peru.
Altitude and health
Cusco sits at 3,400 m (11,150 ft) above sea level. You may experience soroche (altitude sickness).
We recommend resting on the first day, staying hydrated, drinking coca tea or asking about acetazolamide tablets.
Currency and payments
Official currency: the sol (S/). 1 USD ≈ 3.7 to 3.8 soles.
In large cities you can pay by card. In villages and markets, carry cash.
ATMs are common, but check the fees for international withdrawals.
Safety and precautions
Peru is generally safe, but:
Watch your bags, backpacks and phones in crowded areas.
Use app-based taxis or taxis recommended by your hotel.
Carry copies of your documents and keep the originals in a safe place.
Connectivity
Affordable prepaid SIM cards are available from companies such as Claro, Movistar and Entel.
Many rural areas have limited coverage; check whether your hotel offers Wi-Fi.
Plug type and electricity
Voltage: 220 V / 60 Hz
Outlets: Type A (two flat pins), Type C (two round pins) and Type B (three pins).
Tip: Bring a universal adapter if you’re coming from Europe, the US or Asia.
Tipping
Restaurants: Not mandatory, but it’s customary to leave 10% if the service was good (sometimes it’s already included in the bill as “servicio”).
Tour guides: A tip is expected if they give you a good experience (S/10 to S/20 per person).
Taxis: Tipping is not customary.
Hotels: You can give S/5–10 to porters or housekeeping staff.
Language
Spanish is the official language.
Quechua is also spoken in Cusco and the Andean regions.
In tourist areas, many people understand basic English, but it is not widespread.
Internet and connectivity
You can buy prepaid SIM cards from S/10 with data included. Claro, Movistar, Entel and Bitel are the main carriers.
Use apps such as Google Translate or offline Maps if you’re going to rural areas.
Water and food
Don’t drink tap water. Always use bottled or boiled water.
Eat at recommended places or those popular with tourists to avoid an upset stomach.
Bargaining
Bargaining is common at craft markets and fairs (but do it respectfully).
In established shops and supermarkets, prices are fixed.
Public restrooms
Many charge a fee (between S/0.50 and S/1.00).
Always carry coins, toilet paper and hand sanitizer.
Travel insurance
Highly recommended, especially if you plan to go trekking or do adventure activities (such as at Machu Picchu or the Rainbow Mountain).
Business hours
Shops: approx. 9 a.m. – 8 p.m.
Restaurants: lunch from 12:30 p.m., dinner from 7 p.m.
Banks and exchange offices: Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (some open Saturday until noon).
